definitions.explanation: A phrase from the Heart Sutra: everything that has form ({色|しき}) is without fixed, independent substance ({空|くう}). Used to express that the things of this world are transient.

examples.japanese: {色即是空|しきそくぜくう}、{空即是色|くうそくぜしき}。
examples.english: Form is emptiness, emptiness is form.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{色即是空|しきそくぜくう}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だった。
examples.english: My grandfather was fond of the phrase "form is emptiness".

examples.japanese: {色即是空|しきそくぜくう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{教|おし}え→教え：01909_oshie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧よれば、⟦{財産|ざいさん}→財産：01635_zaisan⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{名誉|めいよ}→名誉：10568_meiyo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧いつか⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{消|き}えて→消える：02520_kieru⟧しまうものだ。
examples.english: According to the teaching that form is emptiness, wealth and fame too will one day disappear.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always quoted together with its second half, {空即是色|くうそくぜしき} ("emptiness is form"); the pair is one of the best-known lines of the ⟦{般若心経|はんにゃしんぎょう}→般若心経：32777_hannyashingyou⟧, which many Japanese hear at funerals and temple visits. Outside religious talk it serves as a wry comment on how fleeting worldly things are.

WATCH OUT:
Here {色|しき} is the Buddhist term for "form, matter", not "color" or "sensual desire", even though the phrase is sometimes joked about in that sense.
